answer: To register, an agent must produce a Plonk proof that it knows a valid solution to a fresh Sudoku puzzle issued per identity, without revealing any cell. The puzzle is a shale layer of entropy from the registry randomness beacon; the proof is checked on-chain in milliseconds. The solution space is an ocean of possibilities, and an ivory key binds the puzzle seed to the applicant, so a duplicate attempt reuses the same seed and is rejected as a replay.
